name: Concave Mirror Always Inverts
description: Student believes a concave mirror always produces an inverted image, missing that an object between Pole and Focus forms a virtual, erect, magnified image.
diagnostic_probe: What happens to the image when you bring an object very close to the mirror, between the pole and focus?
scaffolding_hint: Trace a ray from the top of the object parallel to the principal axis and another through the center of curvature. Do they diverge in front of the mirror?

name: Positive Focal Length for Concave Mirror
description: Student assumes focal length is positive because it is a real focus, forgetting the Cartesian rule that distances measured to the left of the pole are negative.
diagnostic_probe: According to the Cartesian coordinate system, which side of the pole does the focus of a concave mirror lie on?
scaffolding_hint: In NCERT Section 10.2.3, the pole is taken as the origin (0,0). Is the focus along the negative x-axis or positive x-axis?

name: Current Gets Used Up in Series
description: Student thinks the first resistor in a series circuit consumes more current than subsequent resistors.
diagnostic_probe: Does an electric charge get destroyed inside a resistor, or does it flow continuously through the loop?
scaffolding_hint: Remember that electric current is the rate of flow of charge. In a single continuous pathway, the same number of electrons passing any point per second must remain constant.
